page.title: Cabane du Mont Fort & Col Termin (2900 m) — Hike Plan

intro_html: Alpine balcony above Verbier with panoramic views of the Grand Combin and Mont Blanc. A classic Valais high-mountain traverse with excellent accommodation at the historic Cabane du Mont Fort hut.

routes.title_html: Verbier (1,500 m) → Cabane du Mont Fort (2,900 m) via Crête du Bec — Classic alpine traverse with panoramic ridge traverse.
bullets_html: Cabane du Mont Fort (2457m) — Hut; refuel & water
Scree field (2800m) — Loose terrain; 1 hour to summit

getting_there.by_pt_html: SBB + Cable car: Train from Geneva to Le Châble (Gare du Châble-Odémaz) via Martigny (2 h total). From Le Châble station, take the Téléverbier cable car (450 m rise, 5 min) up to Verbier (1,500 m). From Verbier, hike begins immediately. Alternative: Train to Martigny, then PostBus 160 directly to Verbier (~40 min). Check SBB.ch and PostAuto for current schedules.
getting_there.by_car_html: From Le Châble or Verbier: Drive south via Route 9 (Val de Bagnes) to Le Châble (parking lot), or continue to Verbier (1,500 m). Parking at Verbier is available near the town center or at the Téléverbier lower station. From Geneva, take A7 south to Martigny, then Route 9 southeast toward Le Châble (45 min from Geneva). Verbier parking: Verbier tourist office has details on paid parking areas near the lifts.

lapse_rate.example_html: Nyon 492 m: 18°C → Cabane 2,900 m: ~2°C (approx. 0.65°C per 100 m); Or from Verbier 1,500 m: 16°C → ~6°C at summit

weather.season_html: July–September is ideal; snow can linger into early July and return by late September. June and early October are possible but avalanche and weather risk increases. Avoid November–May due to avalanche hazard and poor visibility.

takeaways_html: Crowding: July–August weekends see 150–250+ hikers; trail erosion visible; parking chaos 07:00–10:00.
Hut water: Cabane du Mont Fort water reliable mid-June–September; dependent on snowmelt.
Weather: Cross-Alpine exposure to Atlantic and Mediterranean föhn; bimodal wind patterns.

gear.title: Essential
items_html:
• Hiking poles
  • Sun protection (cream + glasses + hat)
  • 2 L water
  • Emergency snacks

safety_html: Scree avalanche: Loose debris 10–50m slides on descent; cascade hazard high.
Ridge exposure: >1000m drops; wind >50 km/h = serious footing risk.
Weather deterioration: Cloud drop in <30 min; temperature swings 15–20°C.
Lightning risk: Isolated summit; strikes peak 13:00–17:00 in summer.
Foot placement: Scree descent risky; ankle/knee injury risk; helmet recommended.
Rockfall from crowds: Peak season creates falling-rock hazard.
Turn back if thunderstorms develop — lightning risk above treeline is extreme.
disclaimer_html: This page is an informal hike plan, not professional mountain-safety advice. Conditions change rapidly. Always check MeteoSwiss and SAC before setting out.
